title: An Alignment Faking Benchmark with Reproducible Experimental Protocols

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: reproducibility is foundational. Packaging the alignment faking protocol as a benchmark prevents each group from spending weeks reconstructing the setup and enables direct comparison of results.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: packaging experimental protocols requires understanding the alignment faking setup deeply. Writing runner scripts and scoring criteria is manageable but requires careful design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: designing standard prompts, scoring criteria, runner scripts, and testing on three models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) is a substantial undertaking but has a clear deliverable.

evidence: Anthropic's alignment faking study (2024) provides the foundational protocol tested across Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4o, Llama 70B, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Anthropic and OpenAI conducted a joint pilot alignment evaluation exercise with reproducible protocols.
Petri 2.0 (Jan 2026) already packages alignment auditing as a reproducible open-source benchmark with standardized scoring.
HELM Safety v1.0 (Stanford) provides standardized safety evaluation including deception tests.

The idea of packaging alignment faking as a reproducible benchmark is partially realized by existing tools, though a dedicated alignment-faking-specific benchmark with runner scripts for open models is not yet published as a standalone package.
